title: The 10 Best RPGs to Play Right Now
description: From Baldur’s Gate 3 and Elden Ring to Clair Obscur and Cyberpunk 2077, these are Neural Critic’s current picks for the best role-playing games available now.
body: RPG has become less a single genre than a family of design philosophies. Some games emphasize dialogue and consequence, others builds and combat, and others the feeling of inhabiting a character inside a believable world. Neural Critic’s current ranking rewards games that make role-playing feel meaningful rather than simply attaching levels and statistics to another genre.\n\nOnly one game from a franchise appears here so the list can represent different approaches to role-playing in 2026.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: A party of adventurers in Baldur’s Gate 3.

contentBlocks.text: Avowed succeeds by giving its regions enough room to explore without confusing size with depth. Quests, dialogue, companions, and combat builds create multiple ways to approach problems, while the tighter structure keeps the adventure moving. It is especially easy to recommend to players who want the decisions and worldbuilding of a larger RPG without a hundred-hour commitment.
contentBlocks.heading: Avowed
contentBlocks.subtitle: A focused fantasy RPG that values density over endless scale

contentBlocks.text: Nioh 3 asks more from the player than most RPGs on this list, but the reward is an unusually expressive combat and build system. Weapons, equipment, skills, and timing allow different approaches to the same challenge, while broader exploration gives the series more room to breathe. It is demanding, dense, and one of 2026’s strongest choices for players who enjoy learning mechanics deeply.
contentBlocks.heading: Nioh 3
contentBlocks.subtitle: Action-RPG depth for players who enjoy mastering systems

contentBlocks.text: Persona 5 Royal makes time itself part of role-playing. School days, friendships, work, exploration, and dungeon planning all compete for a limited calendar, giving ordinary decisions unusual weight. Its style is immediately recognizable, but the lasting appeal comes from how closely character relationships and progression are tied together across a very long campaign.
contentBlocks.heading: Persona 5 Royal
contentBlocks.subtitle: A long RPG whose daily life is as important as its dungeons

contentBlocks.text: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II makes role-playing tangible through reputation, clothing, conversation, skills, social position, and the player’s knowledge of the world. Its deliberate systems can create friction, but that friction makes growth feel earned. Few RPGs are this committed to letting the player become more capable through understanding rather than simply watching numbers increase.
contentBlocks.heading: Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
contentBlocks.subtitle: Role-playing built around learning how to exist in a historical world

contentBlocks.text: Cyberpunk 2077’s strongest modern form combines flexible character builds with some of CD Projekt Red’s best quest writing. Night City gives those choices a setting with enormous personality, while updates and Phantom Liberty strengthened progression and encounter design. Its recovery from launch problems is remarkable, but the reason it belongs here is what the game has become rather than the story of how it got there.
contentBlocks.heading: Cyberpunk 2077
contentBlocks.subtitle: Build freedom and character writing finally match Night City’s ambition
contentBlocks.platforms: PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2

contentBlocks.text: Metaphor: ReFantazio carries familiar Atlus ideas into a world with a different political and emotional texture. Calendar decisions, party relationships, travel, classes, and turn-based battles continually feed into one another. The result is lengthy without feeling directionless, and its cast gives the larger themes enough personality to keep the adventure grounded.
contentBlocks.heading: Metaphor: ReFantazio
contentBlocks.subtitle: Atlus turns social systems and turn-based combat toward a new fantasy world

contentBlocks.text: The Witcher 3 remains one of the genre’s strongest examples of choice working without obvious morality meters. Side quests can become character studies, local tragedies, or uncomfortable compromises, and Geralt’s established identity makes role-playing about interpretation rather than creating a blank slate. Its combat has aged, but the world and writing still justify the journey.
contentBlocks.heading: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
contentBlocks.subtitle: Quest writing that still gives small decisions lasting weight

contentBlocks.text: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 gives turn-based combat unusual immediacy through active dodges and parries while preserving the importance of party builds, abilities, and strategic planning. Its original world and emotional directness make the adventure memorable beyond its battle system. It feels like a modern argument for why turn-based RPGs can still evolve without abandoning what makes them appealing.
contentBlocks.heading: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
contentBlocks.subtitle: A turn-based RPG that keeps the player physically engaged

contentBlocks.text: Elden Ring rarely asks the player to define a character through dialogue, but it creates role-playing through action. Weapons, spells, armor, summons, routes, optional bosses, and the decision to leave a challenge and return later all shape a personal journey. The Lands Between supports an enormous range of approaches without losing a strong authored identity.
contentBlocks.heading: Elden Ring
contentBlocks.subtitle: Role-playing expressed through exploration, builds, and self-directed challenge

contentBlocks.text: Baldur’s Gate 3 remains Neural Critic’s top RPG because choice reaches almost every layer of the experience. Dialogue, relationships, combat positioning, spells, exploration, environmental interactions, and improvised solutions can all change how a situation develops. The game cannot anticipate everything, but it creates the convincing illusion that it is willing to respond when the player tries something unexpected. That generosity is the heart of role-playing.
contentBlocks.heading: Baldur’s Gate 3
contentBlocks.subtitle: The strongest current example of a world reacting to who the player chooses to be

quickRead: A focused fantasy RPG that values density over endless scale
Action-RPG depth for players who enjoy mastering systems
A long RPG whose daily life is as important as its dungeons
conclusion: ==The best RPGs do not all ask the same question. Some ask who you want to become, some ask what you are willing to sacrifice, and others ask how you want to solve the problem directly in front of you. What connects them is the feeling that the player’s decisions matter to the experience rather than merely decorate it.\n\nThat is the standard Neural Critic will use as this ranking evolves.==
conclusionHeading: Role-playing matters when the game responds to the role
